core.title: Seed feature names from the product capability's produce/consume artifact as {verb}-{object}
core.given: A planner is authoring or renaming a feature in a product capability that has produce/consume artifacts
core.then: Derive the name from a produce/consume artifact (the feature seed) as kebab-case {verb}-{object}, where the verb comes from the artifact type's verb list and the object from the artifact's domain or resource.
prefer: Step 1: identify the seed artifact from the product capability's produce/consume entries (the seed is the produce/consume artifact the feature name is derived from)
Step 2: classify the artifact type as event, state, data or config
Step 3: select the verb from that type's verb list (the lists are defined by convention planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type)
Step 4: choose the object from the artifact's domain OR its resource (either is allowed)
avoid: Inventing feature names not traceable to any produce/consume artifact
Using a verb outside the list for the artifact's type
core.why: Seeding names from produce/consume artifacts keeps features traceable to the product capability's contract and gives consistent, predictable verb-object names (also used as the feature URN segment).
evidence: Each feature name maps to an artifact in its product capability's produce/consume list
The verb belongs to the verb list for that artifact's type (event/state/data/config) and the object matches the artifact's domain or resource
verification: A check of this rule validates feature names within the activation scope — the names of features being introduced or renamed in a plan artifact. It does not check unchanged existing feature names (implementing an already-named feature, or editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name, is out of scope). For each in-scope name it confirms: (1) the name maps to an artifact in its product capability's produce/consume list; (2) the verb belongs to the verb list for that artifact's type (event/state/data/config) and the object matches the artifact's domain or resource; (3) the name is kebab-case {verb}-{object}.

The verb lists themselves are owned by the companion verb-selection convention (planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type); this rule's check consumes those lists and does not re-derive or re-check them.

The rule gives no criterion for choosing among several produce/consume artifacts as the seed, or between the artifact's domain and its resource as the object; a check must accept any choice that satisfies the five steps and must not fail an arbitrary but step-compliant choice.

fires: Planner adds a new feature to a product capability whose produce/consume lists artifacts
Planner renames an existing feature in a product capability plan
doesNotFire: Coder implements an already-named feature without changing its name
Editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name
Naming artifacts themselves (covered by artifact naming conventions)

neutralityNotes: This rule is already almost entirely plan-model level: product capability, feature, produce/consume artifacts, and the event/state/data/config taxonomy are cross-stack plan-model concepts present in the closed vocabulary (layout.capability_dir, layout.feature_dir), so they remain in the core rather than becoming profile data. 'kebab-case' is retained in the core because it is a plain-text identifier format that is part of the obligation itself, not a stack mechanism; if a future stack cannot use kebab-case for feature names, a profile key for the identifier case would have to be proposed (none exists today, so none was invented). The companion rule id planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type is a convention-space id, not a stack name, and is kept verbatim. The 'feature URN segment' reuse in why is rule rationale and is not a profile requirement: the rule imposes no URN shape, so urn.feature (a pattern key) is neither needed nor supplied here. The check is scoped to feature names being introduced or renamed (the activation's change facts), matching Bun's doesNotFire for unchanged names. The only genuinely Bun-specific content is the worked examples (the mechanic:.../match:started mappings) and the 'capability/feature YAML' plan-markup mention, all kept in bun.json as the reference realization.
